{{Quote|Our intelligence reports indicate that Moff Zellos was commanding the Imperial forces on Bothawui. We had never before heard his name, and I am confident we will not be hearing it again.|Jedi Knight Gnost-Dural|<ref name="JoMGD" />}}
'''Zellos''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as a [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]. Zellos [[Commanding officer/Legends|commanded]] the [[Battle of Bothawui (Second; Great Galactic War)|second Imperial invasion]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]], an operation that became a drawn-out [[Ground warfare/Legends|ground assault]] against a guerrilla force of [[Republic soldier]]s and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] led by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Belth Allusis]].

Despite impressive Imperial advantages, Bothawui's Republic defenders inflicted considerable damage to the Imperial strike force. Zellos's men eventually defeated the majority of the Republic forces, prompting the Grand Moff to offer Allusis survival in exchange for his surrender. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] refused, and Allusis and his forces were [[Death/Legends|massacred]], but not before they killed a majority of Zellos's forces. The Battle of Bothawui became a tremendous embarrassment for Zellos, who was not heard from again after returning to the Empire.

==Biography==
{{Quote|It must have come as some shock to Moff Zellos, however, to learn that the number of Imperials who had survived was not sufficient to secure control of the shield generator. Zellos was forced to retreat.|Gnost-Dural|<ref name="JoMGD" />}}
The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] Zellos lived during the [[Great Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] and the revitalized [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], serving as an Imperial [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]]. In the initial stages of the war, the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] had targeted the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] in a widely successful campaign. After the Imperial [[Third battle of the Seswenna sector|capture]] of the [[Seswenna sector/Legends|Seswenna sector]], the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] turned his sights toward the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. The first planned target was the [[Bothan Space/Legends|Bothan sector]]; however, the [[First Battle of Bothawui|first Imperial invasion]] of [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Realspace/Legends|Space]] met with disaster, as the Republic had anticipated the move and stationed [[Republic Navy/Legends|its entire fleet]] over [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]] itself.<ref name="Timeline5" />

[[File:Bothawui_imperials.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Zellos plans his assault on the shield generator.]]
This first major Republic victory provoked the Empire to attempt to redeem its losses by mounting a second campaign to take the [[Planet/Legends|planet]], with Grand Moff Zellos commanding the assault. With Imperial [[Warship/Legends|warships]] from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at his command, the Grand Moff led the [[Battle of Bothawui (Second; Great Galactic War)|second invasion]] of Bothan Space, this time intending to [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombard]] Bothawui from [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] were unable to do so, however, as a [[Bothawui planetary shield|powerful]] [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]] protected Bothawui's surface. Zellos's forces&mdash;a fifty thousand-strong Imperial [[Army/Legends|army]]&mdash;instead landed on the planet to engage the Republic defenders and destroy the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]]. The small Republic force of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and soldiers that remained after the first battle at Bothawui was led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Belth Allusis]],<ref name="Timeline5" /> a leading member of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]]<ref name="JoMGD">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Duarl'']]</ref> who developed new tactics and battle plans to combat the Imperials in the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] forests.<ref name="Timeline5" />

Zellos and his advisors believed the battle would be a swift victory for the Empire, and so they sent their [[Troop/Legends|troops]] into battle in direct assaults. This proved to be detrimental to the Imperial forces, as Allusis's tactics and determination allowed the Jedi and his men to repel the [[Imperial soldier]]. For every Republic [[Trooper/Legends|trooper]] [[Death/Legends|killed]], the Empire lost ten. Zellos was eventually forced to call in reinforcements that overwhelmed the Republic defenders, who rallied to Allusis for one final stand. However, before allowing his men to finish them off, Zellos extended an offer of peace to Allusis. The Grand Moff promised to spare the Jedi Master's life if he surrendered, but Allusis refused the offer, and he and his men fought to the death. Before falling, the Republic forces inflicted enough damage on the Imperial army to drive them off Bothawui.<ref name="Timeline5" /> Zellos's invasion was unsuccessful and served as a major morale boost for the exhausted Republic.<ref name="News Article">{{TORweb|url=news/news-article/20091023_001|text=The Battle of Bothawui|nolive=1}}</ref> The Grand Moff's failure on Bothawui later became the focus of a [[Holodocumentary|holorecord]] created by the [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] Jedi Master [[Gnost-Dural]] in the aftermath of the end of the war.<ref name="Timeline5" /> The record was submitted to the [[Jedi Archives (Tython)|Jedi Archives]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] alongside a [[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|journal]] kept by Master Dural during the Great War. The journal also made mention of Moff Zellos and postulated that the Imperial commander would not be seen again after being punished by his Sith superiors.<ref name="JoMGD" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Foolishly, Zelos responded to the resistance by trying to overpower it. With each wave of his men that fell, he increased the number in the next assault, which only increased the death toll in comparable numbers.|Gnost-Dural|<ref name="JoMGD" />}}
Grand Moff Zellos was a little-known<ref name="JoMGD" /> but high-ranking official within the Sith Empire and took part in the Imperial conquest of the galaxy. As the [[Commanding officer/Legends|commanding officer]] during the Battle of Bothawui, Zellos hoped to use his overwhelming numbers to crush the Republic resistance on the planet. However, he and his fellow commanders overestimated their advantage and used simple, straightforward assaults during the battle. This overconfidence was detrimental to their efforts, pushing Zellos to seek reinforcements. When he finally had Allusis and his defenders at his mercy, Zellos offered the Jedi Master peace in exchange for surrender. After his offer was refused, Zellos allowed his forces to kill Allusis and the rest of the Republic troops, inadvertently martyring Bothawui's defenders.<ref name="Timeline5" /><ref name="News Article" />

==Behind the scenes==
Grand Moff Zellos was introduced in the [[Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui|fifth installment]] of the ''[[Galactic Timeline]]'', an [[in-universe]] account of the events leading up to the [[LucasArts]]/[[BioWare]] massively multiplayer online [[Star Wars video games|video game]] titled ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. The timeline is narrated by Kel-Dor Jedi Master Gnost-Dural, whose voice is provided by actor [[Lance Henriksen]].<ref name="News Article" /> Zellos is again mentioned and pictured in [[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']], a book which was included with collector's editions of ''Star Wars: The Old Republic''.<ref name="Collectors">{{TORweb|url=info/faq/game|text=Frequently Asked Questions|oldversion=20111223090049}}</ref> The game and the journal were released on [[December 20]], [[2011]]. ''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'' consistently misspells Zellos's name as "Zelos."<ref name="JoMGD" />
